commands.summary: Relay — bounded data analysis from your terminal.
commands.usage:
Usage: relay [options] [command]

Relay — bounded data analysis from your terminal.

Options:
  -V, --version         output the version number
  --json                print machine-readable JSON instead of tables
  --api-url <url>       Relay API base URL (default:
                        "https://relay.otonieltrejo.com")
  --token <token>       bearer token for privileged deployments
  --no-color            disable ANSI colors
  --verbose             log every HTTP request to stderr
  -h, --help            display help for command

Commands:
  projects              Work with projects
  files                 Work with uploaded files
  sessions              Run analysis sessions
  artifacts             Inspect and download artifacts
  config                Inspect CLI configuration and API health
  introspect [options]  Emit the machine-readable CLI surface
  help [command]        display help for command

Examples:
  $ relay projects list
  $ relay sessions run ses_01abc "which columns correlate?"

flags.name: --json
flags.description: print machine-readable JSON instead of tables

flags.name: --verbose
flags.description: log every HTTP request to stderr

examples: relay sessions run ses_01abc "which columns correlate?"

commands.usage:
Usage: relay projects [options] [command]

List, create, and inspect Relay projects.

Options:
  -h, --help                    display help for command

Commands:
  list                          List all projects
  create [options]              Create a project
  show <projectId>              Show one project
  rename [options] <projectId>  Rename a project
  archive <projectId>           Archive a project
  unarchive <projectId>         Unarchive a project
  delete [options] <projectId>  Delete a project and everything in it
  help [command]                display help for command

Examples:
  $ relay projects list
  $ relay projects create --name "Q3 data"

Usage: relay projects list [options]

List every project visible to this Relay deployment.

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Examples:
  $ relay projects list
  $ relay projects list --json

Usage: relay projects create [options]

Create a new project.

Options:
  --name <name>         project name
  --description <text>  optional description
  -h, --help            display help for command

Examples:
  $ relay projects create --name "Q3 data" --description "Quarterly export"

Usage: relay projects show [options] <projectId>

Show a single project by id.

Arguments:
  projectId   project id (prj_…)

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Examples:
  $ relay projects show prj_01abc

Usage: relay projects rename [options] <projectId>

Rename a project and/or update its description.

Arguments:
  projectId             project id (prj_…)

Options:
  --name <name>         new project name
  --description <text>  new description
  -h, --help            display help for command

Examples:
  $ relay projects rename prj_01abc --name "Q4 data"

Usage: relay projects archive [options] <projectId>

Archive a project: it stays readable but rejects new writes.

Arguments:
  projectId   project id (prj_…)

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Examples:
  $ relay projects archive prj_01abc

Usage: relay projects unarchive [options] <projectId>

Restore an archived project to the active state.

Arguments:
  projectId   project id (prj_…)

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Examples:
  $ relay projects unarchive prj_01abc

commands.summary: Delete a project and everything in it
commands.usage:
Usage: relay projects delete [options] <projectId>

Permanently delete a project with all its files, sessions, conversations, and
artifacts. Requires --yes.

Arguments:
  projectId   project id (prj_…)

Options:
  --yes       confirm the permanent, cascading deletion
  -h, --help  display help for command

Examples:
  $ relay projects delete prj_01abc --yes

Usage: relay files [options] [command]

List, upload, and inspect a project's data files.

Options:
  -h, --help                   display help for command

Commands:
  list <projectId>             List a project's files
  upload <projectId> <path>    Upload a CSV or TSV file
  show <fileId>                Show one file
  download [options] <fileId>  Download an uploaded file
  delete [options] <fileId>    Delete an uploaded file
  help [command]               display help for command

Examples:
  $ relay files list prj_01abc
  $ relay files upload prj_01abc ./data.csv

Usage: relay files list [options] <projectId>

List the files uploaded to a project.

Arguments:
  projectId   project id (prj_…)

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Examples:
  $ relay files list prj_01abc

commands.summary: Upload a CSV or TSV file
commands.usage:
Usage: relay files upload [options] <projectId> <path>

Upload a local .csv or .tsv file to a project.

Arguments:
  projectId   project id (prj_…)
  path        path to a local .csv/.tsv file

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Examples:
  $ relay files upload prj_01abc ./sales.csv

Usage: relay files show [options] <fileId>

Show a single uploaded file by id, including its sha256.

Arguments:
  fileId      file id (fil_…)

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Examples:
  $ relay files show fil_01abc

Usage: relay files download [options] <fileId>

Download an uploaded file's bytes to a local path.

Arguments:
  fileId        file id (fil_…)

Options:
  --out <path>  output path (defaults to the uploaded filename)
  -h, --help    display help for command

Examples:
  $ relay files download fil_01abc --out ./data.csv

flags.name: --out
flags.description: output path (defaults to the uploaded filename)

commands.usage:
Usage: relay files delete [options] <fileId>

Permanently delete an uploaded file. Refused while an analysis session
references it. Requires --yes.

Arguments:
  fileId      file id (fil_…)

Options:
  --yes       confirm the permanent deletion
  -h, --help  display help for command

Examples:
  $ relay files delete fil_01abc --yes

Usage: relay sessions [options] [command]

Create analysis sessions and ask questions in plain language.

Options:
  -h, --help                          display help for command

Commands:
  list <projectId>                    List a project's sessions
  create [options] <projectId>        Create a session bound to a file
  run [options] <sessionId> <prompt>  Ask a question in plain language
  help [command]                      display help for command

Examples:
  $ relay sessions create prj_01abc --file fil_01abc
  $ relay sessions run ses_01abc "which columns correlate?"
examples: relay sessions run ses_01abc "which columns correlate?"

commands.usage:
Usage: relay sessions list [options] <projectId>

List the analysis sessions of a project.

Arguments:
  projectId   project id (prj_…)

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Examples:
  $ relay sessions list prj_01abc

commands.summary: Create a session bound to a file
commands.usage:
Usage: relay sessions create [options] <projectId>

Create an analysis session for one project file.

Arguments:
  projectId        project id (prj_…)

Options:
  --file <fileId>  file id the session analyzes
  --title <title>  session title
  -h, --help       display help for command

Examples:
  $ relay sessions create prj_01abc --file fil_01abc

commands.summary: Ask a question in plain language
commands.usage:
Usage: relay sessions run [options] <sessionId> <prompt>

Send a natural-language prompt to a session. The prompt is translated to ONE
bounded analysis operation (or refused); the kernel never runs model-authored
code.

Arguments:
  sessionId                      session id (ses_…)
  prompt                         the question, quoted

Options:
  --input-artifact <artifactId>  run on a previous derived table instead of the
                                 file
  -h, --help                     display help for command

Examples:
  $ relay sessions run ses_01abc "which columns correlate?"
  $ relay sessions run ses_01abc "correlate these" --input-artifact art_01abc

flags.name: --input-artifact
flags.description: run on a previous derived table instead of the file

examples: relay sessions run ses_01abc "which columns correlate?"
relay sessions run ses_01abc "correlate these" --input-artifact art_01abc

commands.usage:
Usage: relay artifacts [options] [command]

Every analysis output is a durable artifact with full provenance.

Options:
  -h, --help                       display help for command

Commands:
  list <projectId>                 List a project's artifacts
  show <artifactId>                Show an artifact with its provenance
  download [options] <artifactId>  Download an artifact
  help [command]                   display help for command

Examples:
  $ relay artifacts list prj_01abc
  $ relay artifacts download art_01abc

Usage: relay artifacts list [options] <projectId>

List the artifacts of a project.

Arguments:
  projectId   project id (prj_…)

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Examples:
  $ relay artifacts list prj_01abc

commands.summary: Show an artifact with its provenance
commands.usage:
Usage: relay artifacts show [options] <artifactId>

Show one artifact: source file, operation, params, runtime versions, timing,
lineage.

Arguments:
  artifactId  artifact id (art_…)

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Examples:
  $ relay artifacts show art_01abc

Usage: relay artifacts download [options] <artifactId>

Download an artifact's bytes to a local file.

Arguments:
  artifactId    artifact id (art_…)

Options:
  --out <path>  output path (defaults to the artifact filename)
  -h, --help    display help for command

Examples:
  $ relay artifacts download art_01abc --out ./correlation.csv

flags.name: --out
flags.description: output path (defaults to the artifact filename)

commands.summary: Inspect CLI configuration and API health
commands.usage:
Usage: relay config [options] [command]

Show the resolved CLI configuration and check the Relay API.

Options:
  -h, --help      display help for command

Commands:
  show            Show resolved configuration
  status          Check the Relay API health
  help [command]  display help for command

Examples:
  $ relay config show
  $ relay config status

Usage: relay config show [options]

Show the API URL, whether a token is set (never the token itself), and whether a
demo-workspace identity has been saved.

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Examples:
  $ relay config show

Usage: relay config status [options]

Call GET /api/health and summarize the five checks.

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Examples:
  $ relay config status

Usage: relay introspect [options]

Walk the live command tree and emit every command's path, summary, usage, flags,
exit codes, and examples. This output is the T2_CLI authority source; it is
derived, never authored.

Options:
  --json      emit JSON (the only supported format)
  -h, --help  display help for command

Examples:
  $ relay introspect --json
